title: Pro-etale closed support before constructible restriction
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the constant coefficient sheaves and small pro-etale sites with the size conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The direct-image functor $i_*$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], applied termwise to complexes, has a right adjoint. This right adjoint is the total right derived functor $Ri^!_0$ of the sheaf functor $i^!_0N=i^*\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$ [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support], where $i^*,j^*$ are the module inverse images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. No constructibility or boundedness is imposed on objects or on the values of $Ri^!_0$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact for each affine open $V\subset T$, so $j$ is quasi-compact. The canonical structure maps $i^{-1}A_T\to A_Z$ and $j^{-1}A_T\to A_U$ are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], whose coefficient convention explicitly supplies these maps; hence the ringed coefficient hypotheses of the essential-image theorem hold. Thus [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful], and [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] give exactness and full faithfulness of $i_*$, and identify its essential image with the sheaves killed by $j^*$. We make explicit the open-restriction calculation used below. Under the localized-site identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $j^*$ is restriction: in the inverse-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], for $W\to U$ the indexing category has initial object $W\to T$ with the identity $W\cong W\times_TU$, so its opposite has a terminal object and the presheaf inverse image is $N(W)$; this is already a sheaf, with the restricted constant-ring action. By [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], $(j^*j_*G)(W)=G(W\times_TU)=G(W)$, and the counit is this identity. Consequently $j^*$ of the unit $N\to j_*j^*N$ is an isomorphism, inverse to that counit by the adjunction triangle identity. Since $j^*$ preserves kernels by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], the sheaf $\Gamma_ZN=\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$ has $j^*\Gamma_ZN=0$.

For a sheaf $M$ on $Z$, [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] gives $j^*i_*M=0$; for $\Gamma_ZN$ of Step 1 it gives the natural isomorphism $\Gamma_ZN\to i_*i^*\Gamma_ZN$. If $f:i_*M\to N$, naturality of the open unit $\eta$ gives $\eta_N f=j_*j^*(f)\eta_{i_*M}=0$, because $j^*i_*M=0$. The kernel property therefore gives a unique factorization through $\Gamma_ZN$. Composing with its displayed isomorphism and using [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*M,\Gamma_ZN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(M,i^*\Gamma_ZN)=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(M,i^!_0N)$, with the last equality from [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support]. Thus $i_*\dashv i^!_0$ on the whole sheaf categories. These functors are additive: $i_*$ is additive by its sectionwise definition [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], and its right adjoint preserves zero and finite products, hence biproducts and their diagonal/codiagonal formula for addition.

Use the small skeletons in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The constant coefficient sheaf is a sheaf of commutative rings, so [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] supplies K-injective resolutions on $T$ and $Z$ for arbitrary unbounded complexes. In [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] take $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $v=i_*$ and $u=i^!_0$. Step 2 gives $v\dashv u$ and Step 1 gives exactness of $v$, so $i^!_0$ sends K-injective complexes on $T$ to K-injective complexes on $Z$. To apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], take $F=Q_Z\circ (i^!_0)^K:K(T)\to D(Z)$, where $Q_Z$ is localization and the superscript $K$ means termwise application on the homotopy category. This is an exact functor of triangulated categories: additivity preserves the chain-homotopy equation, shifts and the biproduct differential matrix defining each cone in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cited total-derived theorem constructs $Ri^!_0$ and identifies $Ri^!_0N$ with $Q_Z(i^!_0I)$ whenever $N\to I$ is a K-injective resolution on $T$.

Exactness of $i_*$ and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] give its functor on $D(Z)\to D(T)$ by termwise application (also computing $Ri_*$). Let $K$ be any complex on $Z$, let $N$ be any complex on $T$, and choose a K-injective resolution $N\to I$. Step 3 makes $i^!_0I$ K-injective and identifies it with $Ri^!_0N$ in $D(Z)$. The homotopy adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and the two K-injective Hom comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(i_*K,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T)}(i_*K,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z)}(K,i^!_0I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z)}(K,Ri^!_0N).$$
The resolution can be chosen functorially by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; every displayed comparison is natural in $K$ and $N$. These bijections therefore exhibit $i_*\dashv Ri^!_0$ on the whole unbounded derived categories. No bound or constructibility assumption was used.
